correctness.rationale: The leaf-coordinate projection is exactly the polymatroid given by all intersection-rank upper subset sums and nonnegative coordinate constraints; greedy support functions establish sufficiency. Intrinsic normal lengths give the universal upper bound and an attaining symmetric ball. All possible optimal centers are forced to the stated leaf coordinates. A three-ray comparison rigorously eliminates every intermediate subset cardinality, proving the sharp a=b phase and contact counts. Monotone intersection probabilities yield the strict m>=3 cutoff. Positive edge/pair simplex fans reconstruct all positive leaf ranks, proving normal-fan constancy. A standalone support-vertex/facet checker passed 35 independently enumerated integer-parameter scenarios; those finite tests do not replace the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The 2022 m-graph construction and star combinatorial stabilization are credited. The published standard stellohedron record covers the endpoint m=k inradius/contacts, not the continuous weighted phase or the 2-to-3 contact transition inside one fixed normal fan. The published star hypergraphic result handles diameters, not inballs; projected partial-permutohedron inradius uses a different metric tensor. These statements do not imply the claimed weighted intrinsic contact classification; an equivalent broad polymatroid Chebyshev theorem not found remains a concrete residual bibliographic risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent formula under broad polymatroid inball or generalized-permutohedron Chebyshev-center terminology could exist; no complete global bibliographic census was performed.
The terminal unweighted stellohedron radius is already covered by a published exact theorem; novelty is restricted to continuous weighted and fan-identical intermediate phases.
The leaf projection has a published inradius in a different metric; the statement is specific to the lifted intrinsic Euclidean metric.
